name: CalNForm – Calendar & Form Booking Connector
author: beepdigital

sections.description:
CalNForm connects WordPress forms to Google Calendar, Outlook and Microsoft 365, and Zoho Calendar for live availability and appointment booking. Map your form’s customer, date and time fields, connect a calendar account, and configure booking hours, meeting length, start times and the booking window. Customers can receive confirmations and manage their appointment through private rescheduling and cancellation links.

Google Calendar and Google Meet are available with supported accounts. Microsoft Graph calendars, Microsoft Teams, Zoho Calendar and Zoho Meeting have account-specific requirements, and the editor shows what each connected account supports. Use phone or in-person instructions where video is not needed. Form integrations and their supported editions are identified in the flow editor.

Calendar accounts and form plugins are supplied separately. Administrators can connect with Quick connect or their own OAuth app. Quick connect is described under External services. CalNForm does not send telemetry.

CalNForm Pro is a separate add-on with additional flows and booking administration.

External services

CalNForm Quick connect

Quick connect uses https://connect.calnform.com only when an administrator chooses Quick connect for a calendar account. The connector receives OAuth authorization codes, refresh tokens during Google/Zoho renewal, and the site’s callback URL, random sign-in state and one-time public key. It returns tokens encrypted to a one-time site key. It runs in Montréal, Canada, and never stores tokens, calendar data or booking data. Calendar and booking requests go directly from your site to the provider. Microsoft renewal goes directly to Microsoft as a public client. Own-app connections never contact the connector. The optional Check connector button in Settings makes a health request only when clicked, including for sites using their own app. That request sends standard HTTP metadata, but no tokens, calendar data or booking data. There are no automatic health checks or telemetry.
Privacy: https://calnform.com/privacy/
Terms: https://calnform.com/terms/

Requests are made only for the service an administrator configures and connects, or while serving that flow’s availability, booking and management operations. Providers receive the site’s IP address and normal HTTP metadata with API requests. OAuth sign-in takes place on the provider’s website; CalNForm does not receive your account password. The configured OAuth client ID, client secret, redirect URI, authorization code and refresh token are sent to that provider as needed to authorize or refresh access. Access tokens accompany authenticated API requests. Disconnecting with revoke enabled sends the token to Google or Zoho’s revocation endpoint; Microsoft access is revoked through Microsoft account or tenant controls.

Google Calendar and Google Meet

Services: accounts.google.com, oauth2.googleapis.com and www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3. Calendar discovery sends authorization and calendar identifiers. Availability checks send calendar IDs and the requested date/time range. Creating, rescheduling or cancelling a booking sends the calendar/event ID, appointment start/end and time zone, customer name and email, mapped booking details used in the event title/description/location, and attendee/invitation settings. When native Google Meet is selected, Calendar conferenceData requests a Meet conference with the event. When Google Meet is chosen as a separate meeting account, each booking creates one event on that account’s primary calendar, marked free, with the meeting title, start and end and a Meet conference request. It never includes the customer’s name or email. Rescheduling moves that event and cancelling deletes it. There is no independent Meet API request in this edition. Administrative access tests may create and immediately delete a far-future test event. Retries and recovery requests use the same booking identifiers and event data.
Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms
API terms: https://developers.google.com/terms
Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Microsoft Graph, Outlook and Microsoft Teams

Services: login.microsoftonline.com and graph.microsoft.com/v1.0. Calendar discovery sends account authorization and calendar IDs; availability checks send IDs and date/time ranges. Booking creation, updates and cancellation send event/calendar identifiers, customer name/email and attendee details, booking times/time zone, event title/body/location and invitation settings. Native Teams creation is requested through the calendar event’s online-meeting settings when supported. When Microsoft Teams is chosen as a separate meeting account, each booking creates one event on that account’s default calendar, marked free, with the meeting title, start and end and a Teams online meeting. It never includes the customer’s name or email. Rescheduling moves that event and cancelling deletes it. There is no independent onlineMeetings call. Administrator access tests can create and immediately delete a far-future test event. Tokens refresh when needed and booking recovery may repeat event lookups or updates. The editor’s readiness restrictions still apply.
Terms: https://www.microsoft.com/servicesagreement
API terms: https://learn.microsoft.com/legal/microsoft-apis/terms-of-use
Privacy: https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement

Zoho Calendar and Zoho Meeting

Services: the selected regional accounts.zoho.*, calendar.zoho.* and www.zohoapis.* endpoints. OAuth authorization/token exchange and revocation use the selected region. Calendar discovery and availability checks send calendar IDs and requested date/time ranges. Creating, updating or deleting an appointment sends calendar/event identifiers, customer name/email, attendees, booking start/end and time zone, event title/description/location and invitation settings. Native Zoho Meeting is requested through the Calendar event’s conference settings. When Zoho Meeting is chosen as a separate meeting account, each booking reads that account’s calendar list once and creates one event on its default calendar, marked free, with the meeting title, start and end and a Zoho Meeting conference, without invitations. It never includes the customer’s name or email. Rescheduling moves that event and cancelling deletes it. This edition does not call an independent Zoho Meeting endpoint. An explicit access test creates and immediately deletes a far-future event and its meeting without invitations. Token refresh and recovery occur as required. The editor’s readiness restrictions still apply.
Terms: https://www.zoho.com/terms.html
Privacy: https://www.zoho.com/privacy.html

Help and documentation links

Some admin help panels link to outside pages. These are plain links: they open in the administrator’s browser only when clicked, and CalNForm sends no data to these sites.
* Zoho API Console (api-console.zoho.com, api-console.zohocloud.ca and the other Zoho data centres), opened when an administrator sets up their own Zoho OAuth app. Terms: https://www.zoho.com/terms.html Privacy: https://www.zoho.com/privacy.html
* Google Cloud Console (console.cloud.google.com) and Google developer documentation (developers.google.com, developers.googleblog.com), opened when an administrator sets up their own Google OAuth app. Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
* Microsoft Entra admin center (entra.microsoft.com), Microsoft Learn (learn.microsoft.com) and Microsoft account pages (account.live.com, outlook.live.com), opened when an administrator sets up their own Microsoft app or checks account access. Terms: https://www.microsoft.com/servicesagreement Privacy: https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement
* Google Calendar (calendar.google.com), opened to check a calendar’s settings.
* Documentation pages of the supported form plugins (wpforms.com, wpmudev.com, contactform7.com, fluentforms.com, ninjaforms.com, formidableforms.com, docs.gravityforms.com, elementor.com), opened from the form setup help.
* calnform.com and beepdigital.ca, for CalNForm documentation, support and information about CalNForm Pro. Privacy: https://calnform.com/privacy/ Terms: https://calnform.com/terms/

Other network activity

No other remote API, CDN, analytics, licensing or update service is called by this edition. Assets are bundled locally. Customer-selected calendar-copy links open the relevant calendar website in the customer’s browser and include the appointment title, time and description. Email uses WordPress wp_mail and the site’s configured mail transport; CalNForm does not connect to a separate email API.

Source code

CalNForm has no build step. The JavaScript and CSS files in the assets folder are the original, human-readable source and ship exactly as written. The PHP has no compiled or minified parts.
sections.installation:
1. Use WordPress 6.9 or later and PHP 8.2 or later. Install a supported form plugin.
  2. In Plugins > Add Plugin, search for CalNForm and install it, or upload the calnform zip there. Then activate it.
  3. Open CalNForm and create your booking flow. Select the form provider and map the native customer, date and time fields.
  4. Configure the selected calendar provider’s OAuth application, connect the account and choose a writable destination calendar and any conflict calendars.
  5. Set availability, meeting details, notifications and a management page. Review the integration requirements, then activate the completed flow.
  6. Submit a test booking and verify the calendar event and confirmation before publishing the form.
sections.faq:
Do I need a calendar account?

Yes. You supply a supported calendar account and configure OAuth credentials. Your provider’s subscription, permissions and terms apply.

Are bookings sent to an external service?

Yes, to the calendar service you explicitly connect. See External services for the data and triggers. Phone and in-person bookings still create a calendar event.

Does uninstalling delete my data?

No. Data is kept by default. An administrator can enable “Delete CalNForm data when uninstalling” in CalNForm > Settings and save that choice. Only then does deleting the plugin remove this site’s calnform_ options and bookings table. Deactivation does not delete data. Uninstall does not cancel events already held by external calendar services.
sections.changelog:
2.9.8

  • CalNForm updates from WordPress.org only. A copy downloaded from calnform.com no longer checks calnform.com for updates.
  • Tested with WordPress 7.2 and PHP 8.6.
  • French help for saved phone and in-person meetings points to the Rencontres menu.

2.9.7

  • Calendar accounts: the calendar that receives bookings shows ticked and greyed, “Always checked, this calendar receives bookings.”
  • CalNForm screens follow your own WordPress profile language, even when the booking or the site language is different.
  • Add new flow shows the CalNForm header once, with the Flows tab highlighted.
  • Meetings: Google Meet, Microsoft Teams and Zoho Meeting now work with any calendar. Pick a Google, Microsoft 365 or Zoho account you connected under Calendars, and each booking gets its own link. A reschedule moves the meeting, a cancellation deletes it.
  • Meetings: Your own meeting link. Paste a Zoom, Teams or Google Meet room you already use, and every booking gets it, with any calendar.
  • Settings shows one CalNForm Pro card. The Pro previews, badges and menu notices are gone.
  • Deleting CalNForm with “delete data on uninstall” on also removes its cached data.
  • Bookings work on WordPress Playground and other sites that run on SQLite.
  • WPForms: the stock English thank-you message makes way for the booking details. A thank-you message you wrote, or a translated one, stays above them.
  • Security: every request checks its nonce first, then reads only the fields it needs, sanitized.

2.9.6

  • CalNForm Pro is now the complete plugin. When Pro is active, this plugin steps aside and is turned off; your flows, calendars and bookings stay.
  • A site with an old CalNForm Pro that switched itself off now says so, with where to download the current Pro (calnform.com download only).
  • After a Quick connect sign-in, a banner above your calendars names the account that signed in. It no longer squeezes the new card.
  • Saving a form or meeting closes the panel and confirms it on top. A second-language form fills its fields automatically, and “Missing fields” waits until a form is chosen.
  • A meeting type no flow uses yet shows Ready instead of a calendar warning.
  • The Emails step arrives filled in from your site: organization, sender, notification and reply-to addresses.
  • Reconnecting a calendar also comes back with its panel closed and the confirmation on top.
  • French bookings on an English site read Québec style: “jeudi 26 novembre 2026 à 15 h 00”. A French site keeps its own format.

2.9.5

  • Calendar sign-ins and booking links keep working when the WordPress security keys change (some security plugins rotate them). CalNForm now uses its own encryption key, and existing sites switch over by themselves.
  • Teams stays available on Microsoft 365 flows when another saved account is Outlook.com or Google free.
  • A failed Zoho Meeting check is tried again after a few minutes, not a day later.
  • Dashboard > Updates > Check again also checks calnform.com for CalNForm.

2.9.4

  • Lite: delete your booking flow, or archive it if it has booking history, then set up a new one.
  • Calendar accounts: Reconnect always takes you to sign in. Saving without changes now says nothing changed instead of a silent success.
  • Accounts on your own app open on the “Use your own app” tab.

2.9.3

  • Optional “Booking by CalNForm” line under your booking forms. CalNForm asks when you publish your first flow, and you can change it anytime in CalNForm > Settings > Booking credit.

2.9.2

  • Bookings and Reports in Lite show a preview of the Pro screens, with a screenshot that zooms and the feature list beside it.
  • Forminator: the first flow on a brand-new form now publishes instead of going back to the Form step.
  • Microsoft calendar errors name Microsoft’s error code in the booking note.

2.9.1

  • Calendar accounts keep the other calendars that block bookings, like a personal calendar with your vacations. New flows start with them, and each flow can change its own.
  • The account card shows which flows check each calendar.
  • A calendar account whose access can’t be renewed now says “Needs reconnect” everywhere, instead of “Connected”.
  • When the calendar can’t be read, customers see a clear “booking unavailable” message above the date field, instead of a calendar with every day greyed out.
  • Flow wizard: clearer start time setting, fields that appear only when they matter, a review step that lists every choice, and notices that stay inside their step.
  • The second form language tab names its language, or says “Add a language”.

2.9.0

  • Quick connect: connect Google Calendar, Microsoft Outlook or Zoho Calendar in a few clicks, without creating an OAuth app. The CalNForm connector runs in Montréal and stores no calendar or booking data.
  • Your own OAuth app is still available. An account can switch between Quick connect and its own app without relinking flows.
  • Clear messages when a Quick connect sign-in is cancelled, expires, needs admin approval or the account is already connected with your own app.
  • New admin look: light, consistent screens with one control size and spacing system.
  • Calendars, Forms and Meetings open New and Edit in a side panel.
  • One Settings page: data retention, system status and help. The old Pro settings link redirects.
  • System status shows WP-Cron, PHP sodium, HTTPS and Quick connect accounts. “Check connector” contacts connect.calnform.com only when you click it.
  • Calendar rate limits: bookings, reschedules and cancellations back off and retry when a provider is busy, instead of failing.
  • Fixed: a calendar card shows the right edition when the account doesn’t report one.

2.7.9

  • Fixed: unticking a flow option (Test mode, Enable bookings, weekly hours) now saves.
  • Fixed: the booking page no longer fails when a calendar has a zero-length event.
  • Fixed: Forminator booking forms reset properly after a booking.
  • When a calendar returns unreadable busy times, the admin message names the calendar.

2.7.8

  • Settings, Reports and Bookings: each section has its heading above its panel.
  • Buttons follow one style: blue for the main action, outlined for the others, never full width.
  • Fixed: the data retention Save button was white and full width.

2.7.7

  • Calendars, forms and meetings use one card layout: type, edition, status, name and the flows that use them.
  • Edit, duplicate and delete use the same icons everywhere, including flow cards.
  • Blocked actions are greyed out and explain why when you point at them.
  • Flow settings tabs are easier to find and stay visible while you scroll.
  • Fixed: switching tabs no longer shows “Unsaved changes”; links on dark panels are easier to read.

2.7.6

  • Calendar, form and meeting setup now share one panel, in a flow and on their own screens.
  • Picking a saved form or meeting shows it as a card you can change or edit.
  • Flow cards show their calendar, form and meeting at a glance.
  • Better contrast on dark panels; the old booking page shortcode still works.

2.7.5

  • Delete a draft flow, or archive a flow with past bookings so its history stays available.
  • Lite: prepare a new flow while the current one keeps taking bookings, then switch in one step.
  • Clearer progress while creating a flow: green when done, orange to review, red to fix.
  • Saved calendars, forms and meetings look the same everywhere, in the flow and on their own screens.
  • Help opens in a light window; actions ask for confirmation and can’t be clicked twice.
  • Fixed: saving a flow could show “Booking service is busy”; publishing with a saved calendar account now works.

2.7.4

  • New flows are created step by step: Calendar, Form, Meeting, Hours and rules, Emails, Booking page, then Review and publish, with a progress bar, Back and Next.
  • Your progress is saved at every step, so you can leave and pick up where you stopped.
  • Editing screens share one dark look; saved flows, calendars, forms and meetings are listed in light cards.

2.7.3

  • Booking fields are matched by type, so labels like “Available times” just work.
  • Saving your only flow no longer fails.
  • Your destination calendar is no longer listed twice under conflict calendars.
  • Clearer notices, and menus in the same order as the flow: Calendars, Forms, Meetings.

2.7.2

  • Setup help opens in a window with clear tabs, next to each choice.
  • Simpler setup: no needless choices, forms and meetings are named for you.
  • Form check shows a clear verdict and exactly what to fix.
  • Forms with the same name are easy to tell apart.

2.7.1

  • Calendar accounts connect from the setup screen without losing your other settings. A failed save keeps what you entered.
  • Microsoft Outlook, Microsoft Teams and Zoho Meeting are available.
  • One Flows menu. Pro pages explain themselves instead of redirecting.
  • Setup help for every connector.
  • Clearer wording throughout.

2.7.0

  • Prepare the Lite package and service disclosures for WordPress.org submission.
  • Keep data on uninstall unless an administrator explicitly opts into deletion.
